title: Osteoporosis Risk Assessment and Fracture Prevention

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults at risk of fragility fracture: who to assess, FRAX/QFracture and DXA, treatment thresholds and bisphosphonate therapy. Verified against NICE NG259 (Osteoporosis: risk assessment, 2026), NICE TA464 (bisphosphonates) and the Saudi PHA Clinical Preventive Guideline 2023 (DXA); doses from FDA labels.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Vitamin D/calcium supplement doses — local protocol

pathophysiology.summary: Osteoporosis is low bone mass and micro-architectural deterioration causing fragility fractures (from a fall from standing height or less), especially hip, vertebra and wrist.
keyMechanisms: Bone resorption exceeds formation after menopause (oestrogen loss), with ageing and with glucocorticoids.
Low BMD (T-score -2.5 or less) and previous fracture predict future fracture.
Bisphosphonates inhibit osteoclasts and reduce fracture risk.

symptoms: Often silent until fracture; height loss, back pain (vertebral fracture).
physicalSigns: Kyphosis, height loss; low BMI; fall risk.
redFlags: Hip or vertebral fragility fracture — treat
Glucocorticoids 15 mg or more prednisolone daily for 3 months or more — consider treatment (NICE)
precipitants: Low BMI, smoking, alcohol over 14 units/week

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Assess people 50+ and post-menopausal women with previous fragility fracture or glucocorticoid use; consider in men 75+, women 65+, and others with risk factors (NICE)
ruleIn.expectedFinding: High risk of major osteoporotic fracture.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess risk
actions: Use NICE NG259 criteria and Table 1 risk factors; FRAX or QFracture; DXA when it will inform the decision.

clinicalManagement.title: Treat
actions: Consider treatment in people 50+ / post-menopausal women with previous hip or vertebral fragility fracture, very high-dose glucocorticoids, T-score -2.5 or less, or T-score -1.5 or less with fracture, glucocorticoids or bone-loss medicines (NICE 1.7.3).
Bisphosphonates (alendronic acid, ibandronic acid, risedronate, zoledronic acid) are options (NICE TA464); e.g. alendronate 70 mg once weekly (label).
Specialist advice for under-50s with major fracture or rare bone disease (NICE 1.7.5).

clinicalManagement.title: Falls and lifestyle
actions: Falls assessment; stop smoking; limit alcohol; adequate calcium and vitamin D.

learningObjectives: Assess fragility fracture risk and start fracture-preventing treatment when indicated.

Bisphosphonate first line; alendronate 70 mg weekly.
pitfalls: Not treating after a hip or vertebral fracture.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Hip/vertebral fracture; prednisolone 15 mg+ for 3 months+; T -2.5 or less; T -1.5 or less with risk factors
